idiom_name: class-template wrapper or CRTP mixin over a component type; std::function composition over a callable
implementation_notes: C++ has no component value and no reflection, so the enhancer is written by hand: a class template that derives from the wrapped type - a mixin, including the CRTP form documented by cppreference - or a wrapper type that owns a component and forwards calls. Where a component is represented as a callable (a render function), std::function plus generic lambdas compose two callables into a new one, which is the closest C++ gets to the pattern's shape. The template/mixin form is still the right choice when the enhancement must preserve the wrapped type's interface exactly with static dispatch and no allocation, while the callable form fits components that are values handed to a framework anyway.
pitfalls: Object slicing and lifetime: storing or returning the wrapper by value slices the wrapped type unless the mixin derives as above or the component is held polymorphically.
A mixin or forwarding wrapper must forward the base's constructors and must not hide overloaded members; a member that is not forwarded silently disappears from the wrapper's interface.
std::function stores copyable state only: a component capturing move-only state cannot be held in one, so the wrapper has to template on the callable instead.
